<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par125 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּזְרֹעַ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיק}}, if with Delitzsch it is to be referred to God; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּים}} meaning ''important words'', but in 15:13 {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּין|translate=reproachful words}}. Cf. on this point, {{GHGpar|117|q}}, note 3, and Delitzsch, ''Psalmen'', ed. 4, p. 79.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|d}}
'''2.''' Real ''proper nouns'', as being the names of things (or persons) only ''once'' met with, are sufficiently determinate in themselves. Such names, therefore, as {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}}, {{GHGheb|text=דָּוִד}}, {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲקֹב}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּנַ֫עַן}}, {{GHGheb|text=סְדֹם}} do not admit of the article,<ref>Consequently, {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמְנַשֶּׁח}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=1|verse=12}}, &c. (in the Deuteronomist) in the combination {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁבֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה}} (for which elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁבֶט מְנַשֶּׁה}}) is to be regarded ''not'' as a proper name but as a gentilic name (= ''the tribe of the Manassites''), for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=29|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=שׁ׳ הַֽמְנַשִּׁי}} is used, as in 10:8 {{GHGheb|text=שׁ׳ הַלֵּוִי|translate=the tribe of the Levites}}, and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=שּׁ׳ הַדָּנִי|translate=the tribe of the Danites}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=13|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמְנַשֶּׁה}} (like gentilic names in {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}) is even used adjectivally.</ref> nor can they be in the construct state. On the other hand, not only ''gentilic'' names (as denoting the ''various'' individuals belonging to the same class), but also all those proper names, of which the appellative sense is still sufficiently evident to the mind, or at least has been handed down from an earlier period of the language, frequently (often even as a rule) take the article (according to {{GHGpar|126|e}}), and may even be followed by a genitive.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|e}}
Examples. Like the above-mentioned proper names of individuals, countries, and cities, so also national names, which are identical in form with the name of the founder of the race (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׂרָאֵל}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֱדֹם}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוֹאָב}}), are always determinate in themselves. Of gentilic names (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעִבְרִי|translate=the Hebrew}}, {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעִבְרִים|translate=the Hebrews}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַכְּנַֽעֲנִי|translate=the Canaanite}}) the plural {{GHGheb|text=פְּלִשְׁתִּים}}, even when meaning ''the'' Philistines, is generally used without the article (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=7}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=הַפְּ׳}}); so always {{GHGheb|text=כַּפְתֹּרִים}}.—Evident appellatives (like such modern names as ''the Hague'', ''le Havre'') are {{GHGheb|text=הַגִּבְעָה|translate=the hill}}, in the construct state {{GHGheb|text=גִּבְעַת שָׁאוּל}}, i.e. ''the Gibeah named after Saul'' to distinguish it from others; {{GHGheb|text=הָֽרָמָה|translate=the height}}; {{GHGheb|text=הָעַי|translate=the heap}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַלְּבָנוֹן}} (prop. ''the white mountain'') ''the Lebanon''; {{GHGheb|text=הַיְאֹר}} (prop. ''the river'') ''the Nile'', cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=8|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּיאוֹר מִצְרָֽיִם|translate=like the river of Egypt}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַיַּרְדֵּן|translate=the Jordan}} (according to Seybold, ''Mittheil. und Nachr. des DPV.'', 1896, p. 11, probably ''the drinking-place'' [{{GHGheb|text=ירד}}, Arab. ''warada'', meaning orig. ''to go down to drink'']).

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|f}}
Rem. 1. In a few instances original appellatives have completely assumed the character of real proper names, and are therefore used without the article; thus {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים|translate=God}}, to denote the one true God (as elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=יהוה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=1}} and so generally in this document of the Pentateuch up to Ex 6, elsewhere sometimes {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֱלֹהִים}} ὁ θεός (cf. {{GHGpar|126|e}}); also the sing. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלוֹהַּ|translate=God}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֶלְיוֹן|translate=the Most High}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שַׁדַּי|translate=the Almighty}} never take the article.—Moreover, {{GHGheb|text=אָדָם|translate=Adam}} from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=5|verse=1}} onwards (previously in 2:7, &c., {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאָדָם|translate=the}} first ''man''); {{GHGheb|text=שָׁטָן|translate=Satan}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=21|verse=1}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=6}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=הַשָּׂטָן|translate=the adversary}}); cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד|translate=the tent of revelation}} (i.e. the tabernacle), always without the article.

{{GHGmargin-letter|125|g}}
